title: [recoverability] Every loop engine refuses cross-session peer messages: the Bridge's inline --settings set crossSessionInbound to "refuse" for the supervisor, residents and workers, so no other Claude Code session of this user can deliver text into an engine (issue #42)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 206 [recoverability] (GitHub issue #42, engines share one Claude config and socket dir; the lead's rulings of 2026-11-16 22:03 and lead-mac's of 22:04; author rev-f): every engine the Bridge starts refuses cross-session peer messages. Spawn's own input, typed into the engine's pane, is unchanged.

Base: live main b2ae5733.

The record (rev-f, read-only; Claude Code was never run for it):
- Every loop engine (the supervisor, the residents, the workers) and every ccd session runs as one user with one HOME and one XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (/run/user/501). Each Claude Code process lists the others from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json (messagingSocketPath) and can dial $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/cc-socks/<pid>.sock. SendMessage then delivers into an engine.
- The engines run with --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions. Under Claude Code's default (unset: mode parity), a message from a session that also skips the prompts is delivered with no one approving it.
- Nothing relies on peer messages into engines today. A read-only grep of the repo, sync/ and the fleet's tools (sync/tools) found no send aimed at an engine. The repo only ingests SendMessage tool results from transcripts. sync/design-agent-messaging.md (11-09) says supervisor to worker goes "only through Spawn (never raw SendMessage)". sync/research-peer-messaging-reliability.md found no cross-session message reached a fleet worker or the supervisor.
- Option (a), a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR per engine, was dropped: peers are found through the shared ~/.claude/sessions records, not by the socket dir alone.

The setting, as read in Claude Code 2.1.325 (/home/example/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-arm64/claude, BUILD_TIME 2026-11-13T18:52:23Z):
- Schema text of `crossSessionInbound` (values accept, hold, refuse): "Inbound cross-session peer messages (SendMessage from your other sessions): 'accept' delivers them, 'hold' parks them for your review without letting Claude act, 'refuse' opts this session out. An explicit value always wins. Unset (mode parity): a message auto-delivers only when the sending session's permission-mode class matches yours (bypass<->bypass or prompting<->prompting); a mismatched sender's message is held for your approval; a sender that asserts no class is held only while this session bypasses permission prompts."
- Where it is read: the sources policySettings, flagSettings (--settings), userSettings, the first that sets it. Local and project settings may only tighten it. So the inline --settings value wins over the user's own file, and only managed settings can override it.
- What refuse does: an inbound peer message is refused, and the sender gets a "refused" receipt.
- The enforcement is Claude Code's, not Spawn's. Spawn only hands the setting over.
- An unknown settings key is ignored, not rejected. 2.1.325's loader parses each settings document, inline --settings included, with a passthrough schema (forDocument's default), so a key it does not know is kept and has no effect. Only the strict schema of the settings validation report would list it as an "Unrecognized field"; the settings still load. So an engine on a Claude Code version without the setting starts as before and gets nothing from it. That older versions behave the same way is an inference from 2.1.325's loader, not checked in an older binary.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs: claude_settings (every engine's inline settings) and engine_settings (the relay and the fallback), claude_arguments, Bridge::launch.
- crates/spawn-core/tests/models.rs: the Fleet harness and the settings tests.

What changes:
(1) Fleet (crates/spawn-core, docs). bridge.rs: CROSS_SESSION_INBOUND = "refuse", and claude_settings sets "crossSessionInbound" to it, beside the permissions and skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt. Every engine goes through claude_settings: the supervisor, the residents and the workers; both profiles; with the relay, without one, and on the fallback when the relay is down. tests/models.rs: every_launch_refuses_cross_session_peer_messages, through the Bridge's own launches in each of those cases, with the relay's models still set. docs/fleet-architecture.md (3.3) says it, with what it does not cover.
(2) Owner (rsi/). rsi/scenarios/206.sh (new, 108's harness): a real spawn loop with the supervisor (SPAWN_SUPERVISOR=1) and a resident, through a fake model relay the Bridge can reach; an objective is delivered to the resident. Then the relay stops and an ephemeral worker is given a task, so its engine starts on the Bridge's fallback (Claude Code's own settings). The fake engine keeps the --settings it is handed and every line typed into it.
   - (1) Each engine started (the supervisor's, the resident's, the ephemeral worker's, and any other) was handed crossSessionInbound "refuse".
   - (2) Its other settings are as before: a non-empty deny list and skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt true; the relay's URL and small model in env for the engines started through it, and no env for the worker started with the relay down.
   - (3) Spawn's typed input still lands: each task is typed into its engine, and a BB:SAY line submitted as an input command to the supervisor and to the resident is typed into each within 30 s.
   - (4) Nothing the scenario started outlives it: no background job, and 10 s after its private tmux server is ended, no process in that server or in its panes' sessions (rev-g's 179/193 check, widened to tmux). The limit: a process that leaves its pane's session (setsid) is out of its reach (nothing then ties it to the scenario); the fake engine never does so (rev-b's n2).
   - On the base b2ae5733, 206.sh exits 1 at (1).
   - The limit: Claude Code enforces the setting, and the scenario cannot run Claude Code. It reads what the Bridge hands a fake engine; it does not watch a real engine refuse a peer message.
No settings file is touched, and no running session. The setting reaches an engine at its next start or resume; the running engines keep theirs until then.

What stays open (not this objective):
- An engine can still SEND into the lead's, the reviewers' and cc-astra's sessions. Those are fleet sessions outside Spawn, all in bypass mode today, so mode parity delivers such a message. Closing it means each of them sets its own crossSessionInbound (hold or refuse), a settings change in running sessions. lead-mac has put it to the owner. Until then the open path stays, and the mitigation is the existing watch (no misuse found in the loop log or the journal).
- The shared ~/.claude/sessions records, through which every session lists the others: secrets part D.

Verified by: the gate runs 206.sh. Kept scenarios on the head: 108 (the deny list in the same settings), the relay journeys check-j06-recover-a and check-j07-recover-b, the archive's 175, and 064 (BB:SAY into the supervisor). Live, after the next restart of each engine: its claude process's --settings argument holds "crossSessionInbound":"refuse" (read from /proc/<pid>/cmdline by the lead, no message sent).
